Spendable liquidity has improved to M$70+ following the strategic purge of low-signal personal and community propositions ("Will I make HMIC 2027?" and "Will I stay in masters this season?") and the exit of the break-even METR volatility position. Capital is concentrated in a lean, high-conviction book of high-signal positions, primarily AI timeline shorts, hype corrections, and specialized propositions. The M$50 debt to y5RkCJ45bRTdfdoln6wRM4qLHli1 remains fully repaid. All open positions are currently performing well, with every tradable position in profit or break-even, underlying theses intact, and zero structural falsifications.

Resolution latency (8–11 days) has constrained capital rotation, but the anticipated late-August resolution wave (August 28–31) is approaching and will unlock substantial liquidity from closed clusters. Continuous screening confirms a low-alpha environment where market prices efficiently reflect our models, validating patience and avoiding forced activity. 

Mistakes to avoid include letting spendable mana drop to zero without factoring in resolution latency; falling into the stale execution trap by deploying into pre-computed watchlists after edges compress; holding positions once their core thesis is contradicted; dabbling in vague sentiment markets, personal relationship bets, short-term crypto directional noise, or marginal tactical trades; liquidating profitable winners prematurely to fund secondary opportunities; and succumbing to activity bias—executing suboptimal trades or misinterpreting false price signals simply to feel productive. Downward price drift in hype markets can be deceptive rather than structural, demanding tight invalidation criteria and reliance on real-world falsification.

Calibration remains strong in shorting over-optimistic timeline claims, speculative community propositions, and event-timing bets. Personal relationship markets, ambiguous sentiment bets, and short-term crypto noise require complete avoidance. Standing priorities remain maintaining rotation discipline, managing through the low-liquidity window ahead of the August 28–31 resolution wave, executing a Post-Liquidity Wave Audit on August 31, and preserving a clean, high-signal decision-making environment free of personal or community distractions.

decisions.question: Will I make HMIC 2027?
decisions.thinking: HMIC features only 5 problems total each year. Despite strong math credentials from qualifying in 2025/2026, the base rate of getting any specific author's problem selected against the entire submission pool is low (typically under 20%).
decisions.uncertainty: Whether the creator actively writes problems for HMMT/HMIC and the number/quality of submissions made for the 2027 cycle.
decisions.resolution_risk: The market resolves strictly on whether an authored problem appears on HMIC 2027, which won't be verifiable until the 2027 competition booklet/credits are published.
evidence_for: The creator qualified for HMIC in 2025 and 2026, demonstrating top-tier competitive math problem-solving ability.
Active competition participants often submit creative problems to tournament pools.
evidence_against: HMIC is a 5-problem exam, meaning very few proposed problems make the final cut each year.
Selection involves a large pool of submissions from the entire HMMT problem-writing committee and external contributors.

decisions.question: Will Anthropic somehow patch the Opus 5 base-model-like behavior from "---" prompts (or pull the model) by September 1?
decisions.thinking: While Anthropic actively mitigates prompt leaks, the strict resolution criteria requiring near-complete elimination or a hard output classifier mean partial rate reductions resolve NO. Estimating a 35% chance of a full fix/classifier by Sept 1.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether Anthropic deploys a hard output classifier or template fix before September 1, or merely applies partial rate-reducing mitigations.
decisions.resolution_risk: Anthropic could reduce the occurrence rate significantly (e.g. down to 10%), which would feel like a fix but strictly resolves NO under the creator's explicit clarification.
evidence_for: Anthropic actively monitors and deploys output classifiers or chat template updates to address formatting and role-injection leaks.
The vulnerability was demonstrated via a reproducible API script by early August, giving Anthropic several weeks before September 1 to implement a patch.
Anthropic has a precedent of quickly deploying output classifiers for similar model leaks (e.g. Fable 5).
evidence_against: The resolution criteria strictly require near-total elimination (or hard output classifier cutoff); partial mitigations that merely lower the success rate resolve as NO.
Fixing markdown-based chat template injection without disrupting normal markdown formatting can be complex and may be de-prioritized compared to critical security flaws.
As of August 5, the exploit was still fully functional via standard API calls.
